webp.description.message: A tool to convert images to WebP format. Processing happens entirely in the browser, so images are never sent to a server.

webp.subtitle.message: Drag and drop images to convert them to WebP format. Everything runs in your browser — images are never uploaded to a server.

webp.dropHint.message: Drop images here, or click to select

webp.note1.message: Conversion happens entirely in your browser; images are never sent to a server.

webp.note2.message: Use the quality slider to adjust compression (lower values produce smaller files).

webp.note3.message: You can convert multiple images at once.

svgIco.description.message: A tool to convert SVG images to ICO format. Processing happens entirely in the browser, so images are never sent to a server.

svgIco.subtitle.message: Drag and drop SVG images to convert them to ICO format. Selecting multiple sizes packs them all into a single ICO file.

svgIco.dropHint.message: Drop SVG images here, or click to select

svgIco.note1.message: Conversion happens entirely in your browser; images are never sent to a server.

svgIco.note2.message: Selecting multiple sizes packs multiple resolutions into a single ICO file (Windows automatically picks the right one for each icon display size).

svgIco.note3.message: You can convert multiple images at once.

yamlJson.description.message: A tool to convert between YAML and JSON. Processing happens entirely in the browser, so content is never sent to a server.

yamlJson.note1.message: Conversion happens entirely in your browser; content is never sent to a server.

yamlJson.note2.message: Use the swap button to switch between YAML → JSON and JSON → YAML.

yamlJson.note3.message: If there is a syntax error, the error details appear below the result.

base64.encodePlaceholder.description: Placeholder for the encode source textarea

base64.decodePlaceholder.description: Placeholder for the decode source textarea

base64.errorInvalid.message: This string cannot be interpreted as Base64.

base64.binaryNotice.message: Cannot be displayed as text (it may be binary data). The data: URI and download options are still available.

base64.dropHint.message: Drop a file here, or click to select

base64.note1.message: Conversion happens entirely in your browser; content and files are never sent to a server.

base64.note2.message: Pasting a data: URI directly when decoding automatically detects the MIME type.

base64.note3.message: Click [Open in new tab] to view the content directly in the browser via the data: scheme.

base64.note4.message: Dropping a file lets you copy or directly open that file's Base64 and data: URI.

certGen.privateKeyWarning.message: Keep private keys secure and never share them with anyone.

certGen.errorUploadMissing.message: Please provide both the CA certificate and CA private key.

certGen.errorUploadMismatch.message: The CA certificate and CA private key do not match.

certGen.errorUploadParse.message: Failed to load the CA. Check that it is in PEM format, and that the passphrase is correct if the private key is encrypted.

certGen.errorNoCa.message: No CA is loaded for signing. Generate or upload a root CA first.

certGen.description.message: A tool to generate a root CA certificate and server certificate (self-signed certificate) in the browser. Nothing, including private keys, is sent to a server.

certGen.subtitle.message: Generate a root CA certificate and server certificate (self-signed certificate). Everything happens in the browser; nothing, including private keys, is sent to a server.

certGen.caUploadDropHint.message: Drop the CA certificate and CA private key files here, or click to select (a single combined file is also supported)

certGen.caUploadNotCaWarning.message: This certificate is not configured as a CA (basicConstraints: cA=true). It can still sign certificates, but many clients may not trust it.

certGen.sanLabel.message: SAN (Subject Alternative Name, comma or newline separated; supports domain names and IP addresses)

certGen.signModeSelfDesc.message: The simplest method, where the certificate is its own issuer. No CA is required, but browsers and OSes don't recognize the issuer, so a warning appears every time it's accessed. Suited for testing a single server on your own.

certGen.signModeCaGenerated.message: Sign with the generated root CA

certGen.signModeCaGeneratedHint.message: Not ready — generate a root CA above first

certGen.signModeCaDesc.message: Sign with the private key of the CA generated (or uploaded) in the section above. Once the CA certificate is imported into an OS or browser as a trusted root certification authority, every server certificate signed by that CA is trusted without warnings. Suited for issuing and managing certificates for multiple servers or domains under a single CA.

certGen.signModeCaUploadedHint.message: Not ready — upload a CA above first

certGen.signModeCaUploadedDesc.message: Upload the certificate and private key of an existing CA (e.g., one generated in a previous session of this tool, or a CA shared within your team) and sign with it. It works the same way as "Sign with the generated root CA", but lets you reuse a CA that is already imported into a trust store.

certGen.chainCaCertLabel.message: CA Certificate (PEM) — for importing into a trust store

certGen.note1.message: Certificate generation happens entirely in the browser; nothing, including private keys, is sent to a server.

certGen.note2.message: Reloading the page discards the generated keys and certificates, so download them if you need to keep them.

certGen.note3.message: To have a browser or OS trust a server certificate signed by the root CA, the CA certificate must be imported as a trusted root certification authority.

certGen.note4.message: Certificates generated by this tool are intended for local development and testing. Use certificates issued by a certificate authority in production.

hash.errorInsecureContext.message: Computing hashes requires the Web Crypto API, which is unavailable outside HTTPS or localhost.

hash.errorCompute.message: Failed to compute the hash value.

hash.errorCopy.message: Failed to copy. Please select and copy manually.

hash.description.message: A tool to compute hash values (such as SHA-256) for text or files. Processing happens in the browser, so nothing is sent to a server.

hash.subtitle.message: Enter text or drop a file to compute its hash value. Everything happens in the browser; nothing is sent to a server.

hash.dropHint.message: Drop a file here, or click to select

hash.note1.message: Computation happens entirely in the browser; nothing you enter or upload is sent to a server.

hash.note2.message: SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 are supported. MD5 cannot be computed because the browser's standard API (Web Crypto API) doesn't support it.

hash.note3.message: When verifying file integrity, using SHA-256 or a stronger algorithm is recommended.

miniApps.pageDescription.message: A collection of small tools that run entirely in the browser.

miniApps.subtitle.message: A collection of small tools that run entirely in the browser. None of them send any content to a server.

nslookup.errorNetwork.message: Failed to connect to the server.

nslookup.description.message: A tool to look up a domain's DNS records (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CNAME).

nslookup.subtitle.message: Enter a domain name to look up its DNS records (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CNAME).

nslookup.note1.message: Lookups are performed directly from the browser using DNS over HTTPS (Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1) and are not sent to a server.

nslookup.note2.message: Six record types are supported: A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, and CNAME.

nslookup.note3.message: DNS changes may take time to propagate (due to TTL caching), so results may not always reflect the latest configuration.

passwordGenerator.description.message: A tool to generate secure passphrases and passwords. Processing happens in the browser, so nothing is sent to a server.

passwordGenerator.tip1.message: Aim for at least 15 characters. 20 or more is even safer.

passwordGenerator.tip2.message: A long passphrase is stronger than a short, complex password.

passwordGenerator.tip3.message: Use a completely different password for each service. If one leaks, reused passwords on other services can be compromised too.

passwordGenerator.tip4.message: Combining a few unrelated words makes a passphrase that's both long and easy to remember.

passwordGenerator.tip5.message: Generated strings are processed only in the browser and are never sent to a server.

tsvMarkdown.description.message: A tool to convert tab-separated text copied from Excel into a Markdown table. Processing happens in the browser, so nothing is sent to a server.

tsvMarkdown.subtitle.message: Paste a cell range copied from Excel on the left, and the Markdown table appears on the right. Everything happens in the browser; nothing is sent to a server.

tsvMarkdown.note1.message: You can copy a cell range selected in Excel or a spreadsheet and paste it directly (it's treated as tab-separated text).

tsvMarkdown.note2.message: The first row is treated as the header row.

tsvMarkdown.note3.message: A `|` character within a cell is automatically escaped.

tsvMarkdown.note4.message: Conversion happens entirely in the browser; nothing you enter is sent to a server.

whois.errorNetwork.message: Failed to connect to the server. Please try again later.

whois.description.message: A tool to look up WHOIS information (registrant, name servers, etc.) for a domain name.

whois.subtitle.message: Enter a domain name to look up its WHOIS information (registrant, name servers, expiration date, etc.).

whois.note1.message: Lookups are performed server-side using the WHOIS protocol (port 43). No information other than the domain name entered is stored on the server.

whois.note2.message: When the registry and the registrar managing the registrant information use different WHOIS servers, both results are shown.

whois.note3.message: For some domains, registrant information is anonymized by a privacy protection service.
